content:
Jordan (eng-runtime): heads-up, customer cluster hit a throughput drop after driver bump to 537 on a set of RTX3xxx machines.
Maria (eng-ml): rough numbers?
Kevin (bench): pasted a microbench run i did across drivers and cards:
```
RTX3070 (sm86) driver 535: bf16-tc: 4.5k, fp16-tc: 4.4k
RTX3070 (sm86) driver 537: bf16-tc: 3.2k, fp16-tc: 4.4k
A10 (sm86) driver 535: bf16-tc: 5.0k, fp16-tc: 5.0k
A10 (sm86) driver 537: bf16-tc: 4.9k, fp16-tc: 4.9k
A100 (sm80) driver 537: bf16-tc: 6.0k, fp16-tc: 5.9k
```
Kevin (bench): note the 537 regression is pronounced on consumer sm86 silicon, not on datacenter sm86 (A10) nor on sm80.
Jordan (eng-runtime): initial hypothesis: driver 537 changes scheduling / memory coalescing that hurts our BF16 tensorcore kernels on some sm86 chips.
Maria (eng-ml): did you capture perf counters? anything on L2, warp efficiency, regs?
Kevin (bench): ran perf counters. L2 miss rate up ~18% on the bf16-tc path at seqlen 256+; warp occupancy looks similar, but l2 throughput deltas are large.
Ashish (eng-platform): infra note: VMs all reported Driver Version: 537.13 and Compute Capability: 8.6 via nvml. I also saw slight driver minor diffs across hosts.
Jordan (eng-runtime): repro steps I used to validate:
- model: redwood-3b-qat
- seqlen: 256, batch: 4, tokens generated: 512, warmup: 250
- single node, pinned to one GPU, run tracer with per-kernel timings
Maria (eng-ml): potential interaction with KV-cache: our prefetch fastpath increases L2 usage around prefix decode; if bf16 kernel increases register footprint it could squeeze the cache.
Jordan (eng-runtime): our picker logic at boot is basically:
```
sm = probe_sm();
driver = probe_driver_version();
if sm >= 80 and supports_tc_bf16():
  choose = K_TC_BF16
elif seqlen <= 128:
  choose = K_FAST_PREFETCH
else:
  choose = K_DEFAULT
```
Jordan (eng-runtime): that blind "prefer BF16 on SM>=80" is too coarse given the matrix.
Ashish (eng-platform): proposed immediate mitigation: detect (sm==86 && driver>=537 && seqlen>=256) and prefer FP16-TC or reference kernel until we root-cause. Add a canary rollout.
Kevin (bench): forced fp16 path on the same box and got tokens/s back from ~3.2k to ~4.4k. logs saved: /var/tmp/bench/rt-3090-537-fallback.log
Maria (eng-ml): good. let's be conservative: trigger fallback only when L2-miss delta > 15% vs baseline and seqlen >= 256.
Jordan (eng-runtime): agreed. action items:
- Ashish: add a host probe to telemetry that records driver minor and report when sm==86 & driver>=537
- Jordan: implement heuristic guard and feature-flag `sm86_537_fp16_fallback` with 10% canary
- Kevin: add microbench to CI matrix for (sm86, drivers 535,537) with seqlen 64/128/256/512
- Maria: collect Nvidia counters for KV-heavy prompts to feed into diagnosis
- Ashish: pin a few dev rigs to 535 while we triage to avoid developer churn
BenchBot: rolled out feature-flag `sm86_537_fp16_fallback` -> canary 10%
Maria (eng-ml): small observation: at seqlen <= 128 the bf16 path on consumer sm86 is fine even on 537. problem clearly sequence-length sensitive.
Jordan (eng-runtime): so final temporary rule: if sm==86 & driver>=537 & seqlen>=256 & l2_miss_delta>15% -> prefer FP16-TC (or ref path).
Kevin (bench): opened RINF ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-2421 with perf dumps and nvprof traces.
Ashish (eng-platform): i'll also add an infra job that repros this on all consumer sm86 SKUs nightly so we notice regressions earlier.
Jordan (eng-runtime): Maria will draft release note blurb: "Driver 537 may reduce BF16 tensorcore performance on some SM86 consumer GPUs for longer sequence lengths; runtime will fallback to FP16 on affected hosts until drivers/kernels are fixed."
Maria (eng-ml): i'll include a quick diag snippet: `python tools/arch_probe.py --dump` which prints nvml info + chosen kernel with reasoning.
Jordan (eng-runtime): thanks—closing thread for now. reopen if canary flags show false positives. :thumbsup:
